teaser: Our site factory's pipeline needs one repository and one DNS record per request, yet holds power over the whole organisation. Pipelines need ABPs too.
core_idea: A pipeline driven by agents through pull requests is an agent: give it a behaviour policy with reach, undo, limits and boundaries outside its grant.

nodes.label: An organisation-wide grant
nodes.summary: Administration, contents and workflows on every repository, including delete.

nodes.label: No limits on scale
nodes.summary: Any number of repositories; any CNAME, pointing anywhere.

nodes.label: Fixed code used to excuse it
nodes.summary: Locked pipelines relied on other primitives.

nodes.label: A pull request can change the workflow
nodes.summary: The merged workflow inherits the whole grant.

nodes.label: A behaviour policy for a pipeline
nodes.summary: Reach, undo, limit and an enforcing boundary per capability.

nodes.label: Only boundaries bound
nodes.summary: A control must be enforced by something outside the grant.

quotes.text: Why should a pipeline that makes one site per request be able to make five hundred repositories, or thousands of DNS entries?
Here the code does change, by design.
